body:
The Thailand calendar has a block of holidays for each year for the days that are not given by a rule (Buddhist holy days and special holidays), and has none for 2026 and 2027. On master `Thailand()` treats these days as business days:

2026: January 2nd (additional special holiday), March 3rd (Makha Bucha), June 1st (substitution for Wisakha Bucha, Sunday May 31st), July 29th (Asarnha Bucha) and October 16th (additional special holiday in Bangkok, Notification 26/2569, for the IMF and World Bank meetings). Yes, SET did not trade on October 16th, which answers the question on #2686.
2027: February 22nd (substitution for Makha Bucha), May 20th (Wisakha Bucha) and July 19th (substitution for Asarnha Bucha).

The dates are from the Bank of Thailand notifications 31/2568 and 26/2569 (2026) and 37/2569 (2027). SET was closed on all five 2026 dates; the 2027 dates are the Bank of Thailand's. The new test case compares the whole calendar for 2026 and 2027 with the two lists; it fails on master with these 8 missing days and passes with the change.

#2686 had the first four 2026 dates and was closed as stale.

A second commit adds two 2025 days that were also missing: Monday June 2nd and Monday August 11th, 2025, additional special holidays (Bank of Thailand notification 42/2024); `testThailandCalendar` now checks them.
title: Add the 2026 and 2027 Buddhist and special holidays to the Thailand calendar
